# FIG. 6 - Third embodiment with stirring elements

**View:** Perspective view from above and to the front left, as FIG. 1. Outline line work only; the geometry carries no lettering, the numerals listed below being added in the annotation pass. The vibration motor and the air-extraction mechanism are omitted.

**Geometry to be drawn**

The sheet shows three things: one tile, one machine standing on the tile, and two small blocks carried by the machine.

The covering element 36 is the tile, one large plain quadrilateral in perspective filling the lower drawing area, its upper surface lying open to the right of the machine.

The machine is one plain rectangular body standing on a band that runs round its underside, the band alone touching the tile. Both are shown schematically, these forms being a convention for this sheet.

The band's front surface faces the viewer as one unbroken strip across the whole width, drawn deep, its upper and lower edges well apart; its depth is schematic. Its lower edge meets the tile.

The body is drawn broad and tall, its front face turned toward the viewer as a large plain surface. The view being taken from the front left, the body's left-hand end is also presented to the viewer, and on that side the body and the band share one continuous outer edge against the background.

Two small closed blocks, each a stirring element 48, stand on the front face of the body, one to the left of the other with open face between them, each large enough that its own front face holds a point well inside it. They are shown schematically; their number, form and drawn position are a convention for this sheet only, no engagement with the covering element 36 being asserted.

The whole drawing stands well inside the drawing area.

- The vibration device 10 is the whole machine, the body, the band and the blocks together. Identified on that continuous outer edge on the left-hand side, clear of the front faces and of the blocks.
- The covering element 36 is the tile. Identified well inside the open upper surface to the right of the machine, clear of every edge of the tile.
- Each of the two blocks is a stirring element 48. Identified well inside the front face of the left-hand block, clear of its edges.

**Numerals appearing on this figure:** 10, 36, 48

- 10
- 36

content.text: Both untraced statements are gone from the briefs, and no application text was touched.

input.summary: Both findings are fixed with the suggested wording, and both are confined to figure briefs. In FIG. 6 the stirring-element paragraph no longer places the blocks on a named face or says anything about their relationship to the work: it now reads that two small closed blocks, each a stirring element 48, are carried by the machine and drawn on the body, spaced apart, each large enough that its own visible face holds a point well inside it, shown schematically with their number, form and drawn position a depiction convention for this sheet only. The numeral 48 entry follows, targeting well inside the visible face of the left-hand block. In FIG. 3 the second side 16 is now described only as the face at which the view looks straight, appearing as the area within the inner edge, broad enough for a point well inside it to clear the edge, with the continuity characterisation removed, and its bullet reads as the face within the inner edge. I also removed the two sentences in the FIG. 3 brief that assigned bearing contact and the clearance to particular runs of the loop, which the preceding review reported as critical and which had reappeared in the current file. No claim, description passage, drawing description, numeral definition or numeral list changed; FIG. 3 stands at 2567 characters and FIG. 6 at 2272, with every brief inside the length limit.
reasoning: The FIG. 6 wording was substantive despite the schematic label, because where a stirring element sits and whether it touches the work bear directly on the disclosed function of converting vibration into forward motion. The inventor's passage gives the parts and their effect and nothing else, so both the named face and the negative engagement statement had to go rather than be qualified.

Dropping the non-engagement clause is not a licence to depict contact: the brief simply says nothing either way now, which matches a source that says nothing either way, and the application text was already location-neutral in the description and in claim 10.

On FIG. 3 the phrase describing the second side as one plain face bounded by that edge alone and continuous across to the opposite side asserted that the chamber wall is unbroken over its whole extent. The disclosure states only that the air-extraction mechanism is in fluid communication with a chamber on the second side and gives no route, and this application deliberately depicts none, so an unbroken-boundary statement was the kind of claim the sources do not support.
What remains on that sheet is purely locating: the face is the area within the inner edge and is broad enough to hold a point clear of that edge, which is what the numeral needs and nothing more.

I also re-removed the two sentences pinning bearing contact to the horizontal line and the clearance to the vertical line. The last review called that critical, my edit had been reverted in the working copy, and leaving it would reintroduce a circumferential allocation the disclosure never makes, in a view that does not even draw the covering element.

No section of the application needed touching. The Brief Description and the detailed description say only that FIG. 2 is taken through places where the perimeter member 24 bears on the covering element 36 and FIG. 4 at a place where the clearance 34 is present, which asserts that such places exist without saying where around the loop they lie.

input.prior_art_strategy: Unchanged. Claim 1 rests on the rigid low-friction perimeter member at the perimeter of the second side, ending in a bearing face that leaves a clearance admitting ambient air continuously; an air-extraction mechanism whose volumetric rate holds the chamber below atmospheric against that ingress; an all-rigid transmission path with no elastomeric member, foam member or resilient mount interposed; and a bearing face slidable while the differential is maintained. Keeping the drawings silent on where around the loop contact and ingress fall, and on where the stirring elements sit, keeps the depiction inside the claimed scope, which recites the clearance along at least part of the perimeter member and the stirring elements only as carried by the device. The distinctions stand: the compliant holding walls of DE-202021002652-U1 and US-11408462-B2, the blower-fed air cushion of US-10001245-B2, the vibration that reduces the suction-adhering hold in US-4934475-A, and the lifting and cleaning equipment of US-11247858-B2, which delivers no vibration into a laid covering element.

structured_output.summary: Both findings are fixed with the suggested wording, and both are confined to figure briefs. In FIG. 6 the stirring-element paragraph no longer places the blocks on a named face or says anything about their relationship to the work: it now reads that two small closed blocks, each a stirring element 48, are carried by the machine and drawn on the body, spaced apart, each large enough that its own visible face holds a point well inside it, shown schematically with their number, form and drawn position a depiction convention for this sheet only. The numeral 48 entry follows, targeting well inside the visible face of the left-hand block. In FIG. 3 the second side 16 is now described only as the face at which the view looks straight, appearing as the area within the inner edge, broad enough for a point well inside it to clear the edge, with the continuity characterisation removed, and its bullet reads as the face within the inner edge. I also removed the two sentences in the FIG. 3 brief that assigned bearing contact and the clearance to particular runs of the loop, which the preceding review reported as critical and which had reappeared in the current file. No claim, description passage, drawing description, numeral definition or numeral list changed; FIG. 3 stands at 2567 characters and FIG. 6 at 2272, with every brief inside the length limit.
reasoning: The FIG. 6 wording was substantive despite the schematic label, because where a stirring element sits and whether it touches the work bear directly on the disclosed function of converting vibration into forward motion. The inventor's passage gives the parts and their effect and nothing else, so both the named face and the negative engagement statement had to go rather than be qualified.

Dropping the non-engagement clause is not a licence to depict contact: the brief simply says nothing either way now, which matches a source that says nothing either way, and the application text was already location-neutral in the description and in claim 10.

On FIG. 3 the phrase describing the second side as one plain face bounded by that edge alone and continuous across to the opposite side asserted that the chamber wall is unbroken over its whole extent. The disclosure states only that the air-extraction mechanism is in fluid communication with a chamber on the second side and gives no route, and this application deliberately depicts none, so an unbroken-boundary statement was the kind of claim the sources do not support.
What remains on that sheet is purely locating: the face is the area within the inner edge and is broad enough to hold a point clear of that edge, which is what the numeral needs and nothing more.

I also re-removed the two sentences pinning bearing contact to the horizontal line and the clearance to the vertical line. The last review called that critical, my edit had been reverted in the working copy, and leaving it would reintroduce a circumferential allocation the disclosure never makes, in a view that does not even draw the covering element.

No section of the application needed touching. The Brief Description and the detailed description say only that FIG. 2 is taken through places where the perimeter member 24 bears on the covering element 36 and FIG. 4 at a place where the clearance 34 is present, which asserts that such places exist without saying where around the loop they lie.
